standard_prerequisites.name: The I-power torsion submodule M[I^infinity] of a module, as the union of the M[I^n]

standard_prerequisites.name: The torsion-free criterion identifying modules that have no I-torsion
standard_prerequisites.use: Turns the two-sided torsion statement into the vanishing of M/M[I^infinity].

core_obligations: For the first statement, let m in M map to an element of (M/M[I^infinity])[I], and conclude that I m is contained in M[I^infinity] (proof lines 24051-24052).
Write I = (f_1, ..., f_t) and conclude that f_i m lies in M[I^infinity], i.e. I^{n_i} f_i m = 0 for some n_i > 0 (proof lines 24053-24054).
Take N = sum_i n_i + 2 and conclude that I^N m = 0, hence that m maps to zero in M/M[I^infinity], which is the first statement (proof lines 24055-24057).
For the second statement, suppose 0 -> M' -> M -> M'' -> 0 is a short exact sequence with M' and M'' both I-power torsion (proof lines 24060-24062).
Observe that M[I^infinity] contains M', hence M/M[I^infinity] is a quotient of M'' and is therefore I-power torsion (proof lines 24062-24063).
Combine with the first statement and the torsion-free criterion to conclude that M/M[I^infinity] is zero, so that M is I-power torsion (proof lines 24063-24065).
difficulty_reason: The lemma takes a ring R and a finitely generated ideal I of R and asserts two things: that for any R-module M the quotient M/M[I^infinity] has no I-torsion, i.e. (M/M[I^infinity])[I] = 0; and that an extension of I-power torsion modules is again I-power torsion (source lines 24041-24048). The proof of the first statement is an explicit exponent computation. Given m in M whose image lies in (M/M[I^infinity])[I], one has I m contained in M[I^infinity]; writing I = (f_1, ..., f_t), this gives f_i m in M[I^infinity], so that I^{n_i} f_i m = 0 for some n_i > 0, and taking N = sum_i n_i + 2 yields I^N m = 0 (proof lines 24051-24055). Hence m maps to zero in M/M[I^infinity], which is the first statement (proof lines 24056-24057). The second statement is settled by a quotient argument: for a short exact sequence 0 -> M' -> M -> M'' -> 0 with M' and M'' both I-power torsion, one has M[I^infinity] containing M', so M/M[I^infinity] is a quotient of M'' and is therefore I-power torsion; combined with the first statement and the torsion-free criterion this forces it to be zero, so M is I-power torsion (proof lines 24060-24065). The non-routine content is the exponent bookkeeping in the first statement and the two-sided use of the first statement in the second.
